text:
alex: heads up — seeing a reserve leak on us-west1 GPU nodes, 3 nodes with GPUs in RESERVED state even though pods finished about ~30m ago

maria: ugh, that explains the sudden capacity drop and queuing from the batch queue :/

alex: exact symptom: pod finished, node shows GPU reserved, kubelet logs have repeated `failed to release device` errors. sample: `E0302 14:12:23 kubelet_device_plugin.go:278] failed to unwatch device: context canceled`

jia: any recent device-plugin or driver changes rolled last night?

alex: we rolled the rev of our device-plugin (v0.5.3 -> v0.5.4) on the canary pool at 01:00, then it propagated. metric spike lines up with that deploy window.

ben: can we confirm if this is plugin-level or kernel/driver? Which nodes?

alex: nodes: gpu-usw1-spot-{12,23,48}. Node-level dmesg shows nothing obvious. Device plugin logs contain `failed to unregister Resource` before the crashloop.

maria: immediate mitigation: cordon the 3 nodes, drain safely (evict pods), and restart device-plugin daemonset on them. That should free the GPUs. Also consider restarting kubelet if plugin restart doesn't.

jia: oncall runbook note: draining will cause evictions and might thrash small jobs. suggest temporary scaling of dedicated pool to absorb live traffic before drains.

alex: I already bumped dedicated-capacity by 2 gpus to avoid job fails. Will start drain queue now.

opsbot: Incident detection: gpu-reserve-leak-usw1 triggered — 3 nodes impacted, current reserved gpus: 9, reclaimed: 0.

ben: long-term fix candidates: revert plugin change, add a device-plugin healthcheck + self-heal (restart on unregister failures), or handle release in kubelet via lifecycle hook.

maria: also consider updating scheduler to prefer nodes with low "reserve-time" score. We currently only score by free_gpus and network_loc. Add a short-term scoring penalty for nodes with stale reservations so binpacking avoids them.

alex: good call — could add a soft taint and scheduler-affinity rule: when plugin reports stuck reservations > X, add taint `reserved-leak=true:NoSchedule` then let descheduler/opsbot remove it after cleanup.

jia: what's the cost impact? opsbot, what are the queued job counts and RB usage?

opsbot: queued batch jobs increased 2.4x in the last 40m, estimated cost bump if we scale instead of restore: ~$1.8k/day for temp extra spot capacity.

ben: if revert is low risk we should revert and revalidate on canary; if not, deploy plugin fix with extra logging + backoff.

maria: plan: 1) cordon/drain 3 nodes + restart device-plugin on them (immediate) 2) if plugin restart fixes -> uncordon and monitor for 1h 3) if not fixed -> revert plugin to v0.5.3 on canary and roll back 4) scheduler mitigation: add temporary scoring/tag in prod config to avoid suspect nodes (30m infra change) 5) postmortem and add healthcheck and automatic taint choreography.

alex: starting step 1 now. i'll post logs here as I go.

jia: i'll keep paged and coordinate scale ops if drains cause too many evictions.

opsbot: update: device-plugin pods on gpu-usw1-spot-12 restarted, GPUs STILL reported reserved.

alex: trying kubelet restart on spot-12 (ssh + `systemctl restart kubelet`)

ben: keep sequence consistent: plugin restart -> wait 30s -> kubelet restart -> wait 60s -> check `nvidia-smi` and `kubectl describe node` for resourceAllocations.

alex: kubelet restart applied, `nvidia-smi` shows GPUs free on spot-12. `kubectl describe node` shows resources freed.

opsbot: reclaimed GPUs: 3 (spot-12). overall reserved now 6.

maria: proceed with same on -23 and -48. call if behavior differs.

alex: doing -23 now, plugin restart didn't help; kubelet restart freed GPUs again. looks like device-plugin unregister race triggers kubelet leakage until restart.

ben: sounds like the plugin fails to call `Unregister` cleanly and kubelet holds an orphaned reservation. We'll need a fix at plugin side (retry + graceful close) and a safe kubelet path to garbage-collect stale allocations.

jia: after all 3 nodes cleaned, let's revert the rollout on canary and run a correctness test suite (short-run pods + forced termination) before re-rolling.

maria: agreed. also schedule a short-term infra change: add descheduler periodic job to clean nodes with reservations > 10m and no matching pods. That reduces blast radius for next time.

alex: all 3 nodes cleaned, uncordoned. cluster capacity back to normal. monitoring alerts disabled.

opsbot: incident resolved (auto): reserved leak cleared. impact: queued jobs delayed ~12m median, cost delta avoided via temporary scale.

ben: filing a follow-up RFC for plugin hardening and scheduler scoring change. assign owners?

maria: i'll own the scheduler scoring change. ben you take plugin RFC. alex coordinate the rollback test. jia own oncall playbook updates.

alex: thanks all — will open PRs and update this thread with links. :thumbsup:
